name: Sadalbari
description: A star 33 parsecs away, 8.9 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.

radius.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 112748: radius 8.892 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 44.58 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.051) and temperature

temperature.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 112748: effective temperature 5005 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.083)

gravity.source: SIMBAD's compilation of spectroscopic measurements (mesFe_h): log g 2.85 from 2024A&A...682A.145S; the 25 published values span log g 2.5 to 3.05, across which the limb law changes by at most 0.1% of the centre brightness

distance.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 112748: distance 32.531 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.009), at which the luminosity and radius hold

text.card: A star 33 parsecs away, 8.9 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.
text.introduction: Its brightness, measured band by band, gives 45 times the Sun's luminosity at 5,005 K, so 8.892 solar radii.
text.locator: Table 2, HIP 112748: D, Teff, L, Rad, Q

quotes.title: Mu Pegasi
quotes.card: Mu Pegasi or μ Pegasi, formally named Sadalbari, is a star in the northern constellation of Pegasus.
quotes.introduction: The apparent visual magnitude of this star is 3.5, which is bright enough to be seen with the naked eye even on a moonlit night.

radialVelocity.source: SIMBAD's radial velocity for Gaia DR3 1876510592179455744 (quality A), from 2018A&A...616A...7S; Gaia DR3 measures none
